Threagile (see threagile.io for more details) is an open-source toolkit for agile threat modeling, created by Christian Schneider (christian-schneider.net): It allows to model an architecture with its assets in an agile fashion as a YAML file directly inside the IDE. Upon execution of the Threagile toolkit all standard risk rules (as well as individual custom rules if present) are checked against the architecture model. At the time the Threagile toolkit was executed on the model input file the following risk rules were checked:

Risk ruleSTRIDEDescriptionDetectionRating
Some Individual Risk Example
something-strange
Individual risk category		RepudiationSome text describing the risk category...Some text describing the detection logic...Some text describing the risk assessment...
Accidental Secret Leak
accidental-secret-leak		Information DisclosureSourcecode repositories (including their histories) as well as artifact registries can accidentally contain secrets like checked-in or packaged-in passwords, API tokens, certificates, crypto keys, etc.In-scope sourcecode repositories and artifact registries.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Code Backdooring
code-backdooring		TamperingFor each build pipeline component Code Backdooring risks might arise where attackers compromise the build pipeline in order to let backdoored artifacts be shipped into production. Aside from direct code backdooring this includes backdooring of dependencies and even of more lower-level build infrastructure, like backdooring compilers (similar to what the XcodeGhost malware did) or dependencies.In-scope development relevant technical assets which are either accessed by out-of-scope unmanaged developer clients and/or are directly accessed by any kind of internet-located (non-VPN) component or are themselves directly located on the internet.The risk rating depends on the confidentiality and integrity rating of the code being handled and deployed as well as the placement/calling of this technical asset on/from the internet.
Confused Deputy Agent
confused-deputy-agent		Elevation of PrivilegeAn AI agent that acts for its users but reaches data and tools with an identity of its own, a service account or a workload, can do for any user what the agent may do for all of them. The targets check the agent, not the user, so whatever a user asks for, or a prompt injection makes the agent ask for, is allowed.In-scope ai-agent technical assets that act for users, through an incoming communication link with the identity end-user or from a caller used by humans (other than devops links), and reach a technical asset (other than an llm) processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with the identity service-account or workload, either directly or through the tools of an mcp-server technical asset.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the most sensitive technical asset the agent reaches with its own identity. The attack is likely when the agent takes untrusted input, and unlikely otherwise.
Container Base Image Backdooring
container-baseimage-backdooring		TamperingWhen a technical asset is built using container technologies, Base Image Backdooring risks might arise where base images and other layers used contain vulnerable components or backdoors.In-scope technical assets running as containers, other than external entities. To track the risks of all containers at once, use the risk tracking key container-baseimage-backdooring@*.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets.
Container Platform Escape
container-platform-escape		Elevation of PrivilegeContainer platforms are especially interesting targets for attackers as they host big parts of a containerized runtime infrastructure. When not configured and operated with security best practices in mind, attackers might exploit a vulnerability inside an container and escape towards the platform as highly privileged users. These scenarios might give attackers capabilities to attack every other container as owning the container platform (via container escape attacks) equals to owning every container.In-scope container platforms.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Cross-Account Takeover
cross-account-takeover		Elevation of PrivilegeCloud accounts, subscriptions, projects and VPCs isolate workloads and tenants from each other. Access from one of them into another (account A to account B) is granted by cross-account roles, trust policies or resource policies, and a misconfigured grant (too broad principals or rights, or no condition on the calling account) breaks that isolation.Communication links into in-scope technical assets from technical assets in another cloud account, i.e. where the innermost trust boundaries of type network-cloud-provider around the source and the target differ.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the target technical asset itself and of the data assets it processes and stores. The likelihood rises when the source or the target is multi-tenant, as another tenant can then try to abuse the cross-account access.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cross-site-request-forgery		SpoofingWhen a web application is accessed via web protocols Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) risks might arise.In-scope web applications accessed via typical web access protocols by a caller used by humans or a browser, directly or through technical assets forwarding the traffic, like load balancers, reverse proxies and WAFs. Requests of other callers, like a backend or a batch job, come from no browser a forged request could use, and are skipped.The risk rating depends on the integrity rating of the data sent across the communication link. The attack is very likely, likely for DevOps usage, and unlikely when the link is authenticated with a token (token, short-lived-token or long-lived-token), which a browser does not send on its own like a cookie.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
cross-site-scripting		TamperingFor each web application Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) risks might arise. In terms of the overall risk level take other applications running on the same domain into account as well.In-scope web applications.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed in the web application.
Direct IT/OT Communication
direct-it-ot-communication		Elevation of PrivilegeControllers, field devices, HMIs, SCADA servers and engineering workstations of an industrial control system belong into control zones that IT assets reach only through an industrial DMZ. A direct communication link between an IT asset and an asset of a control zone lets attackers who compromise the IT side, which is far more exposed, move straight into the control of the physical process.In-scope OT technical assets (plc, rtu, safety-controller, field-device, hmi, scada-server, engineering-workstation) with a communication link, in either direction, with a technical asset that is neither an OT asset nor in the industrial DMZ (a historian or an asset tagged with industrial-dmz).The risk rating depends on the integrity and availability of the OT asset, and is the highest for safety controllers. The attack is very likely when the other asset is on the internet, and likely otherwise.
DoS-risky Access Across Trust-Boundary
dos-risky-access-across-trust-boundary		Denial of ServiceAssets accessed across trust boundaries with critical or mission-critical availability rating are more prone to Denial-of-Service (DoS) risks.In-scope technical assets (excluding load-balancer) with availability rating of critical or higher which have incoming data-flows across a network trust-boundary (excluding devops usage).Matching technical assets with availability rating of critical or higher are at low risk. When the availability rating is mission-critical and neither a VPN nor IP filter for the incoming data-flow nor redundancy for the asset is applied, the risk-rating is considered medium.
Denial of Service by Encryption Key Deletion
encryption-key-deletion		Denial of ServiceData in cloud storage encrypted with a key from a cloud key management service (like AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault or Google Cloud KMS) can only be decrypted as long as the key exists. Deleting the key, by mistake or by an attacker with enough rights, makes the data permanently unusable.In-scope encrypted cloud technical assets (residing in cloud trust boundaries or tagged with cloud provider tags) storing data assets, which are either tagged as encrypted with a key from a cloud key management service (aws:kms, azure:keyvault, gcp:kms on the asset, a trust boundary around it or its shared runtime) or communicate with a cloud vault or hsm asset. Key stores themselves are excluded.The risk rating depends on the availability rating of the technical asset itself and of the data assets stored, as the deletion destroys the data but does not disclose it.
Excessive Agency
excessive-agency		Elevation of PrivilegeAn AI agent decides on its own which tools to call and with which arguments. An agent that can change critical systems, directly or through the tools of an MCP server, without a human approving the change, does whatever a prompt injection, a hallucination or a misunderstanding makes it do.In-scope ai-agent technical assets with a non-readonly communication link to a technical asset (other than an llm) processing or storing data rated at least as critical in integrity, either directly or through the tools of an mcp-server technical asset. Agents and links tagged with human-in-the-loop are skipped.The risk rating depends on the integrity rating of the technical asset the agent can change. The attack is likely when the agent takes untrusted input, and unlikely otherwise.
Human Use of Machine Identity
human-use-of-machine-identity		RepudiationPeople who call a service with the account of a machine, like an administrator using the credentials of a service account or a client that ships with an API key of its own, act without an identity of theirs. The service cannot tell them apart, nor require a second factor or end their access when they leave, and the secret gets copied to wherever they work.In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local, from a caller used by humans, whose identity is service-account or workload.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely, as secrets in the hands of people leak easily.
Incomplete Model
incomplete-model		Information DisclosureWhen the threat model contains unknown technologies or transfers data over unknown protocols, this is an indicator for an incomplete model.All technical assets and communication links with technology type or protocol type specified as unknown.low
Insecure Control Protocol
insecure-control-protocol		TamperingMost industrial control protocols, like Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, EtherNet/IP or PROFINET, were designed for closed networks: a controller or field device executes every command it receives, without checking who sent it or whether it was changed on the way. Anyone who can send packets to it can write setpoints and outputs, stop it or download a new program.In-scope controllers (plc, rtu, safety-controller) and field-device technical assets with an incoming non-readonly communication link over an industrial control protocol without a secure variant in use (all of them except modbus-security, dnp3-encrypted and opc-ua-encrypted).The risk rating depends on the integrity and availability of the controlled process, and is the highest for safety controllers. The attack is very likely when the sender is on the internet, likely when it is an IT asset, reaches IT or calls across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.
Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
insecure-inter-agent-communication		SpoofingAn AI agent takes the messages of another agent as tasks to act on. When it cannot verify which agent sent a message, because the link is not authenticated or only with a static secret, or cannot rely on the message being unchanged, because the link is not encrypted, anyone who reaches the link can make it act, and a prompt injection in one agent passes on to the next.Communication links that are not process-local between ai-agent technical assets, into an in-scope agent, whose authentication is none, credentials, session-id or long-lived-token, or whose protocol is not encrypted, when the receiving agent processes data rated at least as confidential or critical or can change such an asset, directly or through the tools of an mcp-server technical asset.The risk rating depends on what the receiving agent can do: the most sensitive data it processes or asset it can change. The attack is likely across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise. The rules on missing authentication, long-lived credentials and unencrypted communication may report the same link for the data it carries.
Kubernetes API Write Access
kubernetes-api-write-access		Elevation of PrivilegeA workload whose service account may change resources through the API of its cluster, even narrowly, like creating pods, reading secrets or patching deployments, hands that power to whoever compromises the workload: a pod created with a mounted host path, or a secret read, opens the rest of the cluster.Communication links that are not readonly and not process-local to a container-platform technical asset from a technical asset that is not used by humans, where either is in scope. Links of devops usage, like deployments, are skipped.The risk rating depends on the most sensitive of the platform, the workload and the technical assets sharing a runtime with the workload. The attack is likely when the workload is on the internet or talks to the internet, and unlikely otherwise.
LDAP-Injection
ldap-injection		TamperingWhen an LDAP server is accessed LDAP-Injection risks might arise. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the LDAP server itself and of the data assets processed.In-scope clients accessing LDAP servers via typical LDAP access protocols.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the LDAP server itself and of the data assets processed.
Long-Lived Credentials
long-lived-credentials		SpoofingPasswords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local and is authenticated with long-lived-token, or with credentials by a caller not used by humans, unless the identity of the link is workload. Links authenticated with token are skipped, as the lifetime of the token is not modelled.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely when the caller is on the internet, is used by humans or calls across a network trust boundary, where secrets leak more easily, and unlikely otherwise.
Missing AI Guardrail
missing-ai-guardrail		Elevation of PrivilegeA guardrail screens what reaches a language model or an agent, and what comes back from it, for prompt injection, jailbreaks and data that must not pass, independently of the model. Without one, the instructions of the system prompt are the only defense, and a model follows whatever content convinces it.In-scope llm and ai-agent technical assets that untrusted content reaches (as for prompt injection) through a communication link that no guardrail screens. A link is screened when it comes from an ai-guardrail technical asset, or when the model or agent is one itself or has a link to one. Links from other language models and agents are skipped, as the rule reports a missing guardrail where the content first reaches a model.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the model or agent. The attack is likely when the model or agent talks to the internet directly, and unlikely otherwise.
Missing AI Monitoring
missing-ai-monitoring		RepudiationWhat an AI agent or a language model does depends on what it reads, so it cannot be tested in full before it runs. Without a record of its prompts, its tool calls and its answers in a monitoring system, nobody sees a prompt injection, an agent going astray or a model that drifts, nor can tell afterwards what it did.In-scope ai-agent technical assets, and in-scope llm technical assets not on the internet (self-hosted models), with no communication link to or from a monitoring technical asset.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the agent or model. The attack is likely when the agent or model takes untrusted content, and unlikely otherwise.
Missing Authentication
missing-authentication		Elevation of PrivilegeTechnical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests when the asset processes sensitive data. In-scope technical assets (except load-balancer, reverse-proxy, service-registry, waf, ids, and ips and in-process calls) should authenticate incoming requests when the asset processes sensitive data. This is especially the case for all multi-tenant assets (there even non-sensitive ones). Links over industrial control protocols that cannot authenticate are left to the insecure-control-protocol rule.The risk rating (medium or high) depends on the sensitivity of the data sent across the communication link. Monitoring callers are exempted from this risk.
Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
missing-authentication-second-factor		Elevation of PrivilegeTechnical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests with multi-factor (MFA) authentication when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by humans.In-scope technical assets (except load-balancer, reverse-proxy, waf, ids, and ips) should authenticate incoming requests via multi-factor authentication (MFA) when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by a client used by a human user. Links over industrial control protocols that cannot authenticate are left to the insecure-control-protocol rule.medium
Missing Build Infrastructure
missing-build-infrastructure		TamperingThe modeled architecture does not contain a build infrastructure (devops-client, sourcecode-repo, build-pipeline, etc.), which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks). If the architecture contains custom-developed parts, the pipeline where code gets developed and built needs to be part of the model.Models with in-scope custom-developed parts missing in-scope development (code creation) and build infrastructure components (devops-client, sourcecode-repo, build-pipeline, etc.).The risk rating depends on the highest sensitivity of the in-scope assets running custom-developed parts.
Missing Cloud Hardening
missing-cloud-hardening		TamperingCloud components should be hardened according to the cloud vendor best practices. This affects their configuration, auditing, and further areas.In-scope cloud components (either residing in cloud trust boundaries or more specifically tagged with cloud provider types).The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Missing File Validation
missing-file-validation		SpoofingWhen a technical asset accepts files, these input files should be strictly validated about filename and type.In-scope technical assets with custom-developed code accepting file data formats.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Missing Hardening
missing-hardening		TamperingTechnical assets with a Relative Attacker Attractiveness (RAA) value of 55 % or higher should be explicitly hardened taking best practices and vendor hardening guides into account.In-scope technical assets with RAA values of 55 % or higher. Generally for high-value targets like data stores, application servers, identity providers and ERP systems this limit is reduced to 40 %The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed in the technical asset.
Missing Identity Propagation
missing-identity-propagation		Elevation of PrivilegeTechnical assets (especially multi-tenant systems), which usually process data for end users should authorize every request based on the identity of the end user when the data flow is authenticated (i.e. non-public). For DevOps usages at least the identity of a service account or a workload is required.In-scope service-like technical assets which usually process data based on end user requests, if authenticated (i.e. non-public), should authorize incoming requests based on the propagated end user identity when their rating is sensitive. This is especially the case for all multi-tenant assets (there even less-sensitive rated ones). DevOps usages are exempted from this risk.The risk rating (medium or high) depends on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability rating of the technical asset.
Missing Identity Provider Isolation
missing-identity-provider-isolation		Elevation of PrivilegeHighly sensitive identity provider assets and their identity data stores should be isolated from other assets by their own network segmentation trust-boundary (execution-environment boundaries do not count as network isolation).In-scope identity provider assets and their identity data stores when surrounded by other (not identity-related) assets (without a network trust-boundary in-between). This risk is especially prevalent when other non-identity related assets are within the same execution environment (i.e. same database or same application server).Default is high impact. The impact is increased to very-high when the asset missing the trust-boundary protection is rated as strictly-confidential or mission-critical.
Missing Identity Store
missing-identity-store		SpoofingThe modeled architecture does not contain an identity store, which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks).Models with authenticated data-flows authorized via end user identity missing an in-scope identity store.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the end user-identity authorized technical assets and their data assets processed.
Missing Network Policy
missing-network-policy		Elevation of PrivilegeWithout network policies, every pod of a Kubernetes cluster can reach the pods of a namespace, and its pods can reach the rest of the cluster and beyond: the namespace separates names, not traffic.Execution environment trust boundaries (Kubernetes namespaces) whose network_policy is none, ingress or egress, holding in-scope technical assets that process or store data rated at least as confidential or critical. Namespaces whose network policy is not modelled are skipped.The risk rating depends on the most sensitive technical asset in the namespace. The attack is likely when incoming traffic is not restricted, and unlikely when only outgoing traffic is not.
Missing Network Segmentation
missing-network-segmentation		Elevation of PrivilegeHighly sensitive assets and/or data stores residing in the same network segment than other lower sensitive assets (like webservers or content management systems etc.) should be better protected by a network segmentation trust-boundary.In-scope technical assets with high sensitivity and RAA values as well as data stores when surrounded by assets (without a network trust-boundary in-between) which are of type client-system, web-server, web-application, cms, web-service-rest, web-service-soap, build-pipeline, sourcecode-repository, monitoring, or similar and there is no direct connection between these (hence no requirement to be so close to each other).Default is low risk. The risk is increased to medium when the asset missing the trust-boundary protection is rated as strictly-confidential or mission-critical.
Missing Object-Level Authorization
missing-object-level-authorization		Elevation of PrivilegeA service that acts for its users must check in each request that the user may access the object at hand, like the order or the account the request names. Checking only that the caller is logged in, or that its role may call the operation, lets any user read or change the objects of others by changing an id in the request (BOLA, also known as IDOR).In-scope technical assets other than datastores and assets that forward requests without authenticating them (like load balancers and reverse proxies), processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical, with an incoming communication link whose authorization is none, authenticated-only or function-level, and whose identity is end-user or whose caller is used by humans. DevOps links, which administrators use by role, and links whose authorization is unknown are skipped.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target, one step higher when the link has no function-level authorization either. The attack is very likely when the caller is on the internet, and likely otherwise.
Missing Policy Decision Point Redundancy
missing-policy-decision-point-redundancy		Denial of ServiceServices that externalize their authorization to a policy decision point, for example through the AuthZEN Authorization API, cannot decide a request without it. When it fails, they either deny every request and stop working, or, when they fail open, allow every request.In-scope policy-decision-point technical assets that are not redundant and that in-scope technical assets ask for decisions through communication links that are not process-local.The risk rating depends on the highest availability rating of the services that ask the policy decision point.
Missing Safety System Independence
missing-safety-system-independence		Elevation of PrivilegeA safety instrumented system brings the process into a safe state when the basic process control fails or is attacked. It only does so when it is independent of that control: when assets other than a dedicated safety engineering workstation can change its program, setpoints or outputs, one compromise can disable the control and the safety function together, as the TRITON attack did.In-scope safety-controller technical assets with an incoming non-readonly communication link that is not process-local, from a technical asset other than an engineering-workstation that has no non-readonly communication links to other controllers.The impact is very high, as the safety function protects people. The attack is very likely when the sender is on the internet, likely when it is an IT asset, reaches IT or calls across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.
Missing Vault (Secret Storage)
missing-vault		Information DisclosureIn order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.Models without a Vault (Secret Storage).The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Missing Vault Isolation
missing-vault-isolation		Elevation of PrivilegeHighly sensitive vault assets and their data stores should be isolated from other assets by their own network segmentation trust-boundary (execution-environment boundaries do not count as network isolation).In-scope vault assets when surrounded by other (not vault-related) assets (without a network trust-boundary in-between). This risk is especially prevalent when other non-vault related assets are within the same execution environment (i.e. same database or same application server).Default is medium impact. The impact is increased to high when the asset missing the trust-boundary protection is rated as strictly-confidential or mission-critical.
Missing Web Application Firewall (WAF)
missing-waf		TamperingTo have a first line of filtering defense, security architectures with web-services or web-applications should include a WAF in front of them. Even though a WAF is not a replacement for security (all components must be secure even without a WAF) it adds another layer of defense to the overall system by delaying some attacks and having easier attack alerting through it.In-scope web-services and/or web-applications accessed across a network trust boundary not having a Web Application Firewall (WAF) in front of them.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Mixed Targets on Shared Runtime
mixed-targets-on-shared-runtime		Elevation of PrivilegeDifferent attacker targets (like frontend and backend/datastore components) should not be running on the same shared (underlying) runtime.Shared runtime running technical assets of different trust-boundaries is at risk. Also mixing backend/datastore with frontend components on the same shared runtime is considered a risk.The risk rating (low or medium) depends on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability rating of the technical asset running on the shared runtime.
Sensitive Data Disclosure through Model Output
model-output-disclosure		Information DisclosureWhatever a language model or an agent can read, it can be talked into writing: data in its prompt, in its context window, in the documents it retrieves or in its training data. A model that has confidential data at hand and answers callers from the internet, from users or from another trust zone may hand that data to callers who are not allowed to see it.In-scope llm and ai-agent technical assets that take untrusted input (as the prompt-injection rule defines it) and process, or read from a vector-database technical asset, data rated at least as confidential.The risk rating depends on the confidentiality of the data the model or agent can read. Talking to the internet directly makes the attack very likely, other untrusted input likely.
Unverified Model Supply Chain
model-supply-chain		TamperingModel weights are code in all but name: they decide what the system answers, and some model formats run code when they are loaded. Models that are self-hosted, fine-tuned or pulled from a model registry can be swapped, backdoored or poisoned anywhere between their training and their deployment.In-scope model-registry technical assets, and in-scope llm technical assets that are custom-developed or communicate with a model-registry.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the model, or by the models a registry serves.
Overprivileged Machine Identity
overprivileged-machine-identity		Elevation of PrivilegeA service account or workload identity that the target lets do everything, because it checks only that the caller is authenticated, like a cluster-admin binding, a subscription-wide role or a database owner, gives whoever controls the caller the whole target, while the caller needs only a part of it.In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local and not readonly, whose identity is service-account or workload and whose authorization is none or authenticated-only. Links whose authorization is unknown are skipped.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely when the link crosses a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.
Path-Traversal
path-traversal		Information DisclosureWhen a filesystem is accessed Path-Traversal or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) risks might arise. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.Filesystems accessed by in-scope callers.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data stored inside the technical asset.
Privileged Workload
privileged-workload		Elevation of PrivilegeA workload that runs as a privileged container, mounts a path of its node or shares the node's network, process or IPC namespace is not contained by its container: whoever controls the workload controls the node, the other workloads on it and the credentials of the node's kubelet.In-scope technical assets that are privileged (the field privileged), rated by what runs on the same shared runtimes.The risk rating depends on the most sensitive of the workload and the technical assets sharing a runtime with it, at least medium as the node itself is at stake. The attack is likely when the workload is on the internet or talks to the internet, and unlikely otherwise.
Prompt Injection
prompt-injection		Elevation of PrivilegeA language model cannot tell the instructions of its prompt apart from the data in it. Content that reaches a model or an agent from users, the internet or another trust zone can carry instructions of its own, either directly in a request or indirectly in a document, a web page or a tool response the model reads, and so take over what the model does.In-scope llm and ai-agent technical assets that untrusted content reaches: they are on the internet, are called across a network trust boundary, read from internet assets (directly or through a tool that does), or are sent requests, directly or through other technical assets, by internet assets or clients used by humans.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the model or agent, raised by one step for agents as they act on what they read. Talking to the internet directly makes the attack very likely, other untrusted input likely.
Public Cloud Asset Access
public-cloud-asset-access		Information DisclosureCloud storage and messaging services like object storage buckets or message queues are governed by resource policies and access control lists. A policy with wildcards (like a principal of "*") or an ACL granting access to all users makes the asset public.In-scope cloud technical assets (residing in cloud trust boundaries or tagged with cloud provider tags) processing or storing data assets, that are either tagged as resource-policy governed services (aws:s3, aws:sqs) or are serverless file storage (like file-server), data-lake or message-queue assets, which is how managed cloud storage and queue services are modelled.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed and stored. The likelihood rises when the asset is reachable from the internet (the internet flag of the asset or a communication link from an internet asset).
Publicly Shared Cloud Snapshot
public-cloud-snapshot		Information DisclosureSnapshots and images of cloud disks, databases and virtual machines (like EBS or RDS snapshots and EC2 AMIs) can be shared with all accounts of the cloud provider. A snapshot shared publicly by mistake hands everything stored on the asset to anyone.In-scope cloud technical assets (residing in cloud trust boundaries or tagged with cloud provider tags) storing data assets, that are either tagged as snapshot-capable services (aws:ebs, aws:rds, aws:ec2 for AMIs) or are database or block-storage assets not running as containers.The risk rating depends on the confidentiality of the technical asset itself and of the data assets stored, as a snapshot discloses the stored data but does not alter it.
Push instead of Pull Deployment
push-instead-of-pull-deployment		TamperingWhen comparing push-based vs. pull-based deployments from a security perspective, pull-based deployments improve the overall security of the deployment targets. Every exposed interface of a production system to accept a deployment increases the attack surface of the production system, thus a pull-based approach exposes less attack surface relevant interfaces.Models with build pipeline components accessing in-scope targets of deployment (in a non-readonly way) which are not build-related components themselves.The risk rating depends on the highest sensitivity of the deployment targets running custom-developed parts.
Search-Query Injection
search-query-injection		TamperingWhen a search engine server is accessed Search-Query Injection risks might arise.In-scope clients accessing search engine servers via typical search access protocols.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the search engine server itself and of the data assets processed.
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
server-side-request-forgery		Information DisclosureWhen a server system (i.e. not a client) is accessing other server systems via typical web protocols Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) or Remote-File-Inclusion (RFI) risks might arise. In-scope non-client systems accessing (using outgoing communication links) targets with either HTTP or HTTPS protocol.The risk rating (low or medium) depends on the sensitivity of the data assets receivable via web protocols from targets within the same network trust-boundary as well on the sensitivity of the data assets receivable via web protocols from the target asset itself. Service Registry Poisoning
service-registry-poisoning		SpoofingWhen a service registry used for discovery of trusted service endpoints Service Registry Poisoning risks might arise.In-scope service registries.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical assets accessing the service registry as well as the data assets processed.
Shared Machine Account
shared-machine-account		Elevation of PrivilegeSeveral technical assets that call others with one service account, API key or workload identity share all of its permissions: each can do what any of them needs, and the targets cannot tell them apart.In-scope technical assets with a communication link naming an account that communication links of other technical assets name as well, with the identity service-account or workload. SQL/NoSQL-Injection
sql-nosql-injection		TamperingWhen a database is accessed via database access protocols SQL/NoSQL-Injection risks might arise. Unauthenticated MCP Server

Unbounded Model Consumption
unbounded-model-consumption		Denial of ServiceEvery request to a language model or an agent costs compute and tokens, and an agent can turn one request into many model calls. Unchecked Deployment
unchecked-deployment		TamperingFor each build-pipeline component Unchecked Deployment risks might arise when the build-pipeline does not include established DevSecOps best-practices. Unencrypted Technical Assets
unencrypted-asset		Information DisclosureDue to the confidentiality rating of the technical asset itself and/or the stored data assets this technical asset must be encrypted. unguarded-access-from-internet		Elevation of PrivilegeInternet-exposed assets must be guarded by a protecting service, application, or reverse-proxy.In-scope technical assets (excluding load-balancer) with confidentiality rating of confidential (or higher) or with integrity rating of critical (or higher) when accessed directly from the internet. When either the confidentiality rating is strictly-confidential or the integrity rating is mission-critical, the risk-rating is considered medium. Unnecessary Communication Link
unnecessary-communication-link		Elevation of PrivilegeWhen a technical communication link does not send or receive any data assets, this is an indicator for an unnecessary communication link (or for an incomplete model).In-scope technical assets' technical communication links not sending or receiving any data assets.low

unnecessary-data-asset		Elevation of PrivilegeWhen a data asset is not processed by any data assets and also not transferred by any communication links, this is an indicator for an unnecessary data asset (or for an incomplete model).Modelled data assets not processed by any data assets and also not transferred by any communication links.low

Unnecessary Technical Asset
unnecessary-technical-asset		Elevation of PrivilegeWhen a technical asset does not process any data assets, this is an indicator for an unnecessary technical asset (or for an incomplete model). Unprotected Authorization Decisions

Untrusted Deserialization
untrusted-deserialization		TamperingWhen a technical asset accepts data in a specific serialized form (like Java or .NET serialization), Untrusted Deserialization risks might arise.In-scope technical assets accepting serialization data formats (including EJB and RMI protocols).The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Vector Store Poisoning
vector-store-poisoning		TamperingLanguage models and agents answer and act on what they retrieve from vector stores, for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or as the memory of an agent. Whoever can write into the store decides what the model believes: a poisoned document or memory entry carries false facts or hidden instructions into every answer that retrieves it, long after it was written.In-scope vector-database technical assets that an llm or ai-agent technical asset communicates with.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the models and agents that use the store. The attack is likely when the store is written by an asset that takes untrusted input or sits across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.
Wrong Communication Link Content
wrong-communication-link-content		Information DisclosureWhen a communication link is defined as readonly, but does not receive any data asset, or when it is defined as not readonly, but does not send any data asset, it is likely to be a model failure.Communication links with inconsistent data assets being sent/received not matching their readonly flag or otherwise inconsistent protocols not matching the target technology type.low
Wrong Trust Boundary Content
wrong-trust-boundary-content		Elevation of PrivilegeWhen a trust boundary of type network-policy-namespace-isolation contains non-container assets it is likely to be a model failure.Trust boundaries which should only contain containers, but have different assets inside.low
XML External Entity (XXE)
xml-external-entity		Information DisclosureWhen a technical asset accepts data in XML format, XML External Entity (XXE) risks might arise.In-scope technical assets accepting XML data formats.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed. Also for cloud-based environments the exploitation impact is at least medium, as cloud backend services can be attacked via SSRF (and XXE vulnerabilities are often also SSRF vulnerabilities).
